module.purpose: Defines the type-level and runtime contracts for route matches, match traversal, route-match construction, and route matching options in the router core.
module.summary: This module provides recursive TypeScript utilities for resolving values and match objects by dotted paths, plus a runtime guard that traverses a match value safely. It defines the strongly typed route-match structures used across router states, including route metadata, loader data, params, search state, context, SSR information, and lifecycle status. It also supplies unions and constructors for deriving matches from route trees and documents options for matching pending, fuzzy, case-sensitive, or inclusive-search locations.
module.businessContext: Supports URL routing and data loading for applications using the router. Incorrect match typing or traversal can expose stale, invalid, or incorrectly scoped route data.

MatchRouteOptions
typeShapes.shape:
{
  /**
   * If `true`, will match against pending location instead of the current location.
   *
   * @link [API Docs](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/api/router/MatchRouteOptionsType#pending-property)
   */
  pending?: boolean
  /**
   * If `true`, will match against the current location with case sensitivity.
   *
   * @link [API Docs](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/api/router/MatchRouteOptionsType#casesensitive-property)
   *
   * @deprecated Declare case sensitivity in the route definition instead, or globally for all routes using the `caseSensitive` option on the router.
   */
  caseSensitive?: boolean
  /**
   * If `true`, will match against the current location's search params using a deep inclusive check. e.g. `{ a: 1 }` will match for a current location of `{ a: 1, b: 2 }`.
   *
   * @link [API Docs](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/api/router/MatchRouteOptionsType#includesearch-property)
   */
  includeSearch?: boolean
  /**
   * If `true`, will match against the current location using a fuzzy match. e.g. `/posts` will match for a current location of `/posts/123`.
   *
   * @link [API Docs](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/api/router/MatchRouteOptionsType#fuzzy-property)
   */
  fuzzy?: boolean
}

detail.name: isMatch
detail.signature: export const isMatch = <TMatch, TPath extends string>(match: TMatch, path: Constrain<TPath, IsMatch<TMatch, TPath>['path']>): match is IsMatch<TMatch, TPath>['result']
preconditions: The path argument is a string constrained by the IsMatch type relationship.
postconditions: Returns true exactly when every traversed segment resolves without encountering a nullish intermediate value and the final resolved value is non-nullish.
Returns false when traversal encounters a nullish value before or at the final segment.
invariants: Path segments are traversed from left to right.
The match value is not mutated.
edgeCases: A path containing multiple dot-separated segments traverses nested properties in order.
A missing property or a nullish intermediate property causes the function to return false.
An empty path is split into a single empty-string property segment and returns whether that property on the match value is non-nullish.

errorPolicy.returnsOnError: Returns false when property traversal reaches a nullish value.

detail.summary: Checks whether a dot-delimited property path resolves to a non-nullish value on the supplied match object. Traversal stops when a path segment is absent or an intermediate value is nullish.

specLiterals.role: Delimiter used to split the property path into traversal segments.

specTests.then: It returns false without attempting traversal beyond the nullish profile value.
It returns true because the resolved value is an empty string, which is non-nullish.
